english.quote: IELTS Academic; IELTS UKAI Academic | Overall score - 6.5 Writing - 6.5, Speaking - 6.5 | TOEFL / TOEFL iBT Home Edition | Total Score - 90 or 4.5 Writing – 25 or 4.5 Verbal/Speaking – 25 or 4.5 | SAT | Total score – 1250 Reading and Writing – 60
english.how_found: Search (ntu.edu.sg only): 'NTU undergraduate admissions international qualifications English language requirement IELTS TOEFL SAT' -> old URL .../admission-guide/international-qualifications/other-international-qualifications (HTTP 404) -> General Admission Requirements page -> link 'Other International Qualifications' -> section 'English Language Requirements' (table cells copied from raw HTML; ' | ' separates cells).
english.notes: Condition sentence on the same page: 'Applicants must submit one of the following English language proficiency tests if English is not the medium of instruction in their high school studies, or if English is presented as a Second Language (ESL) or an Additional Language (EAL) on their academic transcript.' Identical figures appear in the 'English-language proficiency requirements' table on the General Admission Requirements page (https://www.ntu.edu.sg/admissions/undergraduate/admissions/general-admission-requirements#international-qualifications), so no conflict between the OIQ-specific and the general page (both IELTS 6.5). TOEFL is printed as '90 or 4.5' (legacy 0-120 total alongside the newer 1-6 band scale, as printed). SAT 'Reading and Writing – 60' is recorded exactly as printed; the SAT section scale is 200-800, so this may be a typo on NTU's page - not corrected here. Validity (same page): 'For IELTS, TOEFL, PTE Academic, C1 Advanced, and AST, only test scores obtained within two (2) years prior to the application deadline will be accepted. SAT, ACT and MUET scores are valid for five (5) years from the test date.' General page: 'English language proficiency test results must be submitted by the application deadline for the relevant admission exercise. Late submissions will not be considered.' Other accepted tests on the page: PTE Academic Overall 55 (Speaking 55, Writing 59); C1 Advanced 170; ACT with Writing Composite 30/English 30/Writing 7; IGCSE/O-Level First Language English Grade B or 6. Search snippets mentioned older country-specific NTU pages (Thai, Taiwan) with IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL 90 - not read, not verified, and not the OIQ category.

value.description: Published 'Minimum Requirement to Apply' for the applicant's exact qualification, Kazakhstan NIS Grade 12 Certificate (listed as 'Suitable to be considered for Direct Admission: Yes'): score of A in all subjects taken at the NIS Grade 12 Certificate exam. No SAT total or GPA threshold is published for this category; SAT appears only as an English-proficiency option (Total 1250). NTU adds that meeting minimum requirements does not guarantee admission.

gpa.notes: Competitiveness statement on the same page (Note 2): 'Admission is highly competitive, particularly for international applicants, due to the limited number of places available. Admission standards vary from year to year and across programmes. Meeting the minimum application requirements does not guarantee admission to any programme at NTU.' A separate row 'High School Certificate (Kazakhstan)' (non-NIS) is marked 'No, required additional qualification (see below)' - i.e. needs at least 3 AP tests with grades 4-5 or at least 3 GCE A-Level subjects. Programme page adds: 'A strong foundation in Mathematics or Physics or Computing'. Applicants must also meet the programme's Minimum Subject Requirements for International Qualifications (linked from the general page; not read).

deadline.quote: All other international qualifications not listed below (including German Abitur, Turkish High School, New Zealand NCEA, Bangladesh HSC, Pakistan HSC, Iran High School Diploma etc.) | Open | 15 Oct 2026 - 20 Jan 2027
deadline.how_found: Search (ntu.edu.sg only): 'NTU undergraduate admissions application period international qualifications deadline' -> 'General Admission Requirements' (https://www.ntu.edu.sg/admissions/undergraduate/admission-guide/international-qualifications, redirects to the URL given) -> section 'Application windows' table (columns 'International qualifications/admission requirements' | 'Application status' | 'Application window' | 'Deadline for Document submission'). AY label from the Admissions landing page https://www.ntu.edu.sg/admissions/undergraduate/admissions found in the same search.
deadline.notes: This is the AY2027 (August 2027 intake) cycle, not a 2026 date: the Admissions page lists '15 October 2026 | Application for AY2027 opens for students with international qualifications (including IB Diploma)'. Kazakhstan NIS is not listed separately in the table, so it falls under 'All other international qualifications not listed below' (window 15 Oct 2026 - 20 Jan 2027); the OIQ page states 'The application is now OPEN.' Conflict to note: the Admissions landing page gives a generic window 'International qualifications ... 15 October to 19 March 2027 (Depending on the specific international qualifications)' - the 19 March 2027 date applies to other listed qualifications (e.g. IB, American HSD, India Std 12), not to the OIQ group. Supporting documents: 'Upload/Submit documents according to the Checklist within 3 days after application closing date.' Also note NTU writes 'We offer one intake per academic year, with the first term typically commencing in late July' (not August). Final results must be uploaded within 3 days of release or by 31 July at the latest; AP scores (if used) by 15 July 2027.

tuition.how_found: Programme page footer link 'Tuition Fees' -> /admissions/undergraduate/financial-matters/tuition-fees (redirects to the URL given) -> table 'Tuition fees for Academic Year 2026/2027'. Also surfaced by search 'NTU undergraduate tuition fees international students without Tuition Grant Computer Science'. Cohort page https://www.ntu.edu.sg/admissions/undergraduate/fees-and-funding/tuition-fees/accepted-programme-offer-in-2026 shows the same figures.
tuition.notes: Table heading: 'Tuition fees for Academic Year 2026/2027'. Column order as printed: 'Singapore Citizens1' | 'Singapore Permanent Residents1' | 'ASEAN IS2,3 (inclusive of GST)' | 'All Other IS2 (inclusive of GST)' | Non-Subsidised Students2 (not receiving tuition grant) (inclusive of GST): 'Lab Based' | 'Non-Lab Based'. Computer Science is not listed among the exceptions (Accountancy/Business group incl. 'Business & Computing' double degree, Medicine, Renaissance Engineering), so it falls under 'All Programmes (except for those listed below)'. 'amount' is left null because NTU publishes two non-subsidised (without MOE Tuition Grant) figures - S$40,600 Lab Based and S$36,350 Non-Lab Based - and no official page or PDF read defines which programmes are lab-based; the with-grant international figure is unambiguous (S$21,400). Footnote: 'For ASEAN IS and all other international students on subsidised tuition fees and students of all nationalities on non-subsidised tuition fees, the fee amounts quoted are inclusive of 9% GST. GST on the tuition fee is to be borne by students.' Fees are cohort-based: 'For full-time undergraduate programmes, the fees are fixed for your entire candidature under a cohort-based system.' (2026 cohort page: 'Annual tuition fee is fixed at the 2026 rate for the duration of the degree programme.'). AY2027/28 fees (the applicant's cohort) were not published as of 2026-10-17; AY2026/27 is the latest. Tuition Grant for international students carries a 3-year work bond: 'Permanent Residents and international students who accept the MOE tuition grant are required to sign the Tuition Grant Agreement, which obliges you to work for a Singapore entity for three (3) years upon graduation.'

scholarship_exists.quote: The Nanyang Global Scholarship is awarded to outstanding freshmen pursuing undergraduate programmes and recognizes students with outstanding academic results, demonstrate strong leadership abilities, and very good co-curricular records.
scholarship_exists.how_found: Search (ntu.edu.sg only): 'Nanyang Scholarship undergraduate eligibility international students NTU' -> first result (URL slug 'nanyang-scholarship', redirects from /scholarships/scholarship-opportunities/... to /scholarships-and-awards/...); page h1 'Nanyang Global Scholarship'.
scholarship_exists.notes: The page heading is 'Nanyang Global Scholarship' (the URL slug and older references use 'Nanyang Scholarship'). Eligibility: 'Possess outstanding academic achievements in the Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level, Diploma awarded by a polytechnic in Singapore, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma or Year 12 equivalent qualifications.' Application: 'Applicants are required to submit their application for admission before submitting their application for scholarship.' For applicants with Year 12 equivalent results the scholarship application period is the same as the admission application period. Benefits (per page summary): full coverage of subsidised tuition fees (after Tuition Grant), living allowance S$6,500 per academic year, accommodation allowance up to S$2,000, travel grant up to S$8,000, one-off computer allowance S$2,000.

scholarship_international.how_found: Same Nanyang Global Scholarship page -> 'Eligibility' section, first bullet.
scholarship_international.notes: Supporting sentence on the same page: 'No bond is attached to the Nanyang Global Scholarship apart from the three-year bond applicable to all Singapore PRs and international students under the MOE Tuition Grant Scheme.' - i.e. international awardees hold it together with the MOE Tuition Grant (the award covers subsidised fees after Tuition Grant), so the 3-year Singapore work bond applies to them.

access_notes: The WebFetch summariser paraphrases and caps quotes at 125 characters; to obtain verbatim text I downloaded the raw HTML of each cited page with curl (no login, no robots bypass) and extracted text locally. All quotes above are copied from that extracted text; ' | ' marks table-cell boundaries.

URL redirects observed (cited URLs are the effective ones): .../admission-guide/international-qualifications -> .../admissions/general-admission-requirements#international-qualifications; .../financial-matters/tuition-fees -> .../fees-and-funding/tuition-fees; .../scholarships/scholarship-opportunities/detail/nanyang-scholarship -> .../scholarships-and-awards/scholarship-opportunities/detail/nanyang-scholarship; .../financial-matters/tuition-fees/accepted-programme-offer-in-2025 -> .../fees-and-funding/tuition-fees/accepted-programme-offer-in-2025.

Tuition: no official definition of 'Lab Based' vs 'Non-Lab Based' programmes was found on the tuition pages or in the fee PDFs read (AY2025 fee PDF, fee-guidelines PDF, misc-fees AY2026 PDF, important-notes 2022 PDF), so the without-grant amount is given as two published figures. AY2027/28 fees are not yet published.
The tuition page links its 'earlier cohort' pages to a wcms-prod-admin.ntu.edu.sg host (CMS admin host); I used the public www.ntu.edu.sg equivalents instead.
